Which of the following species is neither hypervalent nor hypovalent?
questions.explanation:
Explanation


\t
\tOctet Rule: Atoms tend to gain, lose, or share electrons to achieve a stable electron configuration with eight valence electrons.   
\t
\t
\tHypervalent: Central atom has more than eight valence electrons.
\t
\t
\tHypo-valent: Central atom has less than eight valence electrons.   
\t


Concept


\t
\tWe need to find the species where the central atom has exactly eight valence electrons.
\t



\t
\tClO₄⁻: Cl has 7 valence electrons. In ClO₄⁻, Cl forms 4 bonds (often depicted as double bonds for formal charge minimization), giving it effectively more than 8 electrons. (Hypervalent)
\t
\t
\tBCl₃: B has 3 valence electrons. In BCl₃, B forms 3 bonds, giving it only 6 valence electrons. (Hypovalent)
\t
\t
\tSO₄²⁻: S has 6 valence electrons. In SO₄²⁻, S forms 4 bonds (often depicted as double bonds for formal charge minimization), giving it effectively more than 8 electrons. (Hypervalent)   
\t
\t
\tCO₃²⁻: C has 4 valence electrons. In CO₃²⁻, C forms 4 bonds (one double, two single), giving it exactly 8 valence electrons.
\t

questions.question: Which of the following pair of compounds are isostructural ?
questions.explanation:
Explanation


\t
\tIsostructural compounds have the same shape and arrangement of atoms (same molecular geometry), regardless of the elements involved. This is determined by the number of bond pairs and lone pairs of electrons around the central atom (VSEPR theory).   
\t


Concept


\t
\tAnalyze the structure of each pair:
\t



\t
\tCO₂ and SO₂:

\t
\t\t
\t\tCO₂: Central C has 2 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs → Linear shape.   
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tSO₂: Central S has 2 bond pairs and 1 lone pair → Bent (V-shaped) shape.   
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tNot isostructural.
\t\t
\t
\t
\t
\tSiF₄ and SF₄:

\t
\t\t
\t\tSiF₄: Central Si has 4 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs → Tetrahedral shape.   
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tSF₄: Central S has 4 bond pairs and 1 lone pair → See-saw shape (distorted tetrahedron).
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tNot isostructural.
\t\t
\t
\t
\t
\tXeF₂ and I₃⁻:

\t
\t\t
\t\tXeF₂: Central Xe has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs → Linear shape.   
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tI₃⁻: Central I has 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs → Linear shape.   
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tIsostructural.
\t\t
\t
\t
\t
\tSF₆ and XeF₆:

\t
\t\t
\t\tSF₆: Central S has 6 bond pairs and 0 lone pairs → Octahedral shape.   
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tXeF₆: Central Xe has 6 bond pairs and 1 lone pair → Distorted octahedral (or capped octahedron) shape.
\t\t
\t\t
\t\tNot isostructural.
\t\t
\t
\t


Answer option 3, (XeF₂ and I₃⁻).

questions.question:
Which of the following is not correctly matched:-
        Bond angle         Number of bond angles
(1)  CH4 →  109°28'      →  6
(2)  SF6  →  90°            →  12
(3)  IF7    → 90°             →  10
(4)  IF5    → 90°             →   8
questions.explanation:
Explanation


\t
\tBond angles and their count depend on the molecular geometry.
\t


Concept


\t
\tCH₄ (Tetrahedral): Bond angle is 109°28'. Number of bond angles = 6. (Correct)
\t
\t
\tSF₆ (Octahedral): Bond angles are 90° and 180°. There are 12 bond angles of 90°. (Correct)
\t
\t
\tIF7 (Pentagonal Bipyramidal): Bond angles are 90° (axial-equatorial), 72° (equatorial-equatorial), and 180° (axial-axial). There are 10 bond angles of 90° (5 above and 5 below the equatorial plane). (Correct)
\t
\t
\tIF₅ (Square Pyramidal): Bond angles are approximately 90° (axial-equatorial) and less than 90° (due to lone pair repulsion). There are four basal-axial bond angles (nominally 90°) and four basal-basal bond angles (less than 90°). The statement says 8 bond angles of 90°, which is incorrect angles are not 90°.
\t


Answer option 4, (IF₅ → 90° → 8).

questions.question: Identify correct match Type of overlappingBond formed Internuclear axis (1)px + pxπX(2)px + dxzπX(3)py + dxyπX(4)s + pzπX
questions.explanation:
Explanation


\t
\tSigma (σ) bonds are formed by head-on overlap along the internuclear axis. Pi (π) bonds are formed by sideways overlap of atomic orbitals perpendicular to the internuclear axis.
\t


Concept


\t
\tInternuclear axis is X. This means the bond is forming along the X-axis.
\t
\t
\t(1) px + px along X-axis: This results in head-on overlap, forming a σ bond, not a π bond.
\t
\t
\t(2) px + dxz along X-axis: The px orbital is along the X-axis. The dxz orbital has lobes in the XZ plane. Sideways overlap is not possible, forming a σ bond.
\t
\t
\t(3) py + dxy along X-axis: The py orbital is along the Y-axis. The dxy orbital has lobes between the X and Y axes. Sideways overlap is possible, forming a π bond.
\t
\t
\t(4) s + pz along X-axis: The s orbital is spherical. The pz orbital is along the Z-axis. There will be no effective sideways overlap to form a π bond along the X-axis. forming a σ bond, not a π bond.
\t


Answer option 3

questions.question: Which have linear shape :-
questions.explanation:
Explanation


\t
\tLinear shape occurs when the central atom has two bond pairs and zero lone pairs, resulting in a bond angle of 180°.
\t


Concept


\t
\tXeF₂: Xe has 8 valence electrons. It forms 2 bonds with F, using 2 electrons. This leaves 6 non-bonding electrons or 3 lone pairs. Arrangement is trigonal bipyramidal, but shape is linear (F-Xe-F) due to lone pairs occupying equatorial positions.
\t
\t
\tI₃⁻: The central I has 7 valence electrons. It forms 2 bonds with other I atoms and has a negative charge (1 extra electron), totaling 10 electrons. This means 2 bond pairs and 3 lone pairs. Arrangement is trigonal bipyramidal, but shape is linear (I-I-I) due to lone pairs occupying equatorial positions.
\t
\t
\tCO₂: C has 4 valence electrons. It forms 2 double bonds with O atoms, using all 4 electrons. This means 2 bond pairs and zero lone pairs. Shape is linear (O=C=O).
\t


Answer option 4,(All).

questions.question: If the shortest wavelength of spectral line of H-atom in Lyman series is x, then match the following for Li2+. (A)Shortest wavelength in Lyman series(P)(B)Longest wavelength in Lyman series(Q)(C)Shortest wavelength in Balmer series(R)(D)Longest wavelength in Balmer series(S)
questions.explanation:
A: Question Explanation -  
Match shortest/longest wavelengths for Lyman & Balmer series of Li²⁺ given shortest Lyman wavelength of H is x.

B: Concept ;  
Rydberg formula for hydrogen-like ions.

C: SOLUTION;   
Rydberg equation: 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/n₁² − 1/n₂²).
For H (Z = 1),  for  shortest wavelength of Lyman series (n₂= ∞, n₁=1) ; 1/x = R ⇒ R = 1/x.
Now for Li²⁺ (Z = 3):

for shortest lyman line n₂= ∞, n₁=1 , 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/1² − 1/∞²)= 9/x, 

 λ= (x/9) → R

For Longest Lyman (2 → 1) , 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/1² − 1/2²)  = 27/4x,

So,   λ =4x/27 → S.
For Shortest Balmer (∞ → 2) ,  1/λ = R · Z² · (1/2² − 1/∞²) = 9/4x

So ,  λ =4x/9 → Q.
For Longest Balmer (3 → 2) , 1/λ = R · Z² · (1/2² − 1/3²) = 5/4x

So , λ  = 4x/5 → P.

(A)–R, (B)–S, (C)–Q, (D)–P

D: Final Answer — Option 1
